mechanism_narrative: The recent collapse in WORKPLACES mobility signals weaker commuting and less daytime circulation, which reduces incidental retail visits with a lag. If WORKPLACES stays below its prior four-week average, RETAIL_REC will fall over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC averages higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining depressed or declining further.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after several weeks of weakness diverts discretionary time away from malls and dining districts, lowering retail-and-recreation visits within one to two weeks. The effect is strongest when PARKS turns positive after being negative.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after PARKS turns positive, or instead rises while PARKS remains above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT stays depressed, people are spending more time near home and making fewer city-center shopping trips. That home-centric pattern should push RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and TRANSIT remains below baseline for most of the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp improvement in TRANSIT mobility indicates looser movement constraints and easier access to shopping areas, which should lift RETAIL_REC within one week. The signal is the change in TRANSIT, not its level alone.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the following week after a TRANSIT rebound of at least 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC over the same month indicates broader outing intensity and more errand bundling, which supports additional discretionary shopping trips. Under that interaction, RETAIL_REC should continue rising over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days even while GROCERY_PHARM remains flat or rises from its current level.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and TRANSIT both stay below baseline, the city is in a low-discretionary-mobility regime that usually precedes weaker retail footfall. That regime should suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days while both PARKS and TRANSIT stay negative.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in WORKPLACES from a deep trough should precede more lunchtime and after-work retail visits as office activity normalizes. The effect should appear over four weeks after WORKPLACES stops falling.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two consecutive weeks after a decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES posts two consecutive weekly increases.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL is high and GROCERY_PHARM stays near baseline, households are substituting local, utility-focused trips for discretionary shopping. That pattern should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above 8 points while GROCERY_PHARM stays between -5 and 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 7 days while RESIDENTIAL stays high and GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline.
